what_its_for: Besifloxacin is an antibiotic eye drop used to treat bacterial pink eye (conjunctivitis). It works by killing the bacteria causing the infection in your eye.
how_to_take: Wash your hands well before using. Shake the bottle gently before each use. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to make a small pocket, and squeeze one drop into the pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes. Do not touch the tip of the bottle to your eye, fingers, or any surface to keep it clean. If you wear contact lenses, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in.
dosing: The usual dose is 1 drop in the affected eye(s) 3 times a day, about 4 to 12 hours apart, for 7 days. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use extra drops to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not wear contact lenses while you have signs of eye infection such as redness or discharge. Avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface to prevent contamination. Do not share this medication with others even if they have the same symptoms. Avoid rubbing your eyes after using the drops.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe eye pain, vision changes, increased redness or swelling of the eye, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call if your symptoms do not start to improve after a few days of treatment.
when_it_works: You may start to feel improvement within the first 1 to 2 days of treatment. However, it is very important to use all 7 days of medication even if your eye feels better, to make sure the infection is completely gone.
special_populations: Safety and effectiveness in children under 1 year of age have not been established. Pregnant or breastfeeding patients should talk to their doctor before using this medication. Older adults can generally use this medication safely, but always inform your doctor of all other medications you are taking.
